दिएका छन् । अमेरिकाको भर्जिनियास्थित अदालतमा जारी सुनुवाइका क्रममा उनले यस्तो दाबी गरेका हुन् । अदालतमा आफ्नै प्रतिरक्षामा साक्षीका रूपमा प्रस्तुत भएका नरेशले आफू १३–१४ वर्षको हुँदा माओवादी विद्रोहीले अपहरण गरेको बताए । माओवादीको नियन्त्रणमा दुईदेखि तीन साताभन्दा बढी समय रहँदा आफूले शारीरिक, यौन तथा मानसिक दुर्व्यवहार भोगेको उनको भनाइ छ । बाल्यकालमा भोगेको उक्त घटनाले आफूलाई अहिले पनि मानसिक रूपमा असर गरिरहेको नरेशले बताएका छन् । ती अनुभवबारे कुरा गर्दा आफूलाई नराम्रो महसुस हुने गरेको पनि उनले बयान दिएका छन् । नरेशले बयानकै क्रममा बाल्यकालमा आफ्नी फुपूले आत्मदाह गरेको घटना देखेको र भाइ हराउँदा आफूले त्यसका लागि दोषी महसुस गरेको पनि सुनाएका थिए । आफू मानसिकरूपमा स्वस्थ नरहेको पुष्टि गराउने प्रयासस्वरूप उनले यी प्रसंग सुनाएका हुन् । नरेशमा पीटीएसडी रहेको मनोवैज्ञानिकको निष्कर्ष नरेशको प्रतिरक्षा पक्षले अदालतमा मनोवैज्ञानिक डा. ब्यारी रोजेनफेल्डलाई साक्षीका रूपमा प्रस्तुत गरेको थियो । रोजेनफेल्डले नरेशको मूल्याङ्कनपछि उनमा पोस्ट ट्रमाटिक स्ट्रेस डिसअर्डर (पीटीएसडी) रहेको निष्कर्ष सुनाएका छन् । पीटीएसडी गम्भीर आघातजन्य घटना भोगेपछि विकसित हुन सक्ने मानसिक स्वास्थ्यसम्बन्धी अवस्था हो । यसका लक्षणमा दुःस्वप्न देखिने, पुराना घटनाको सम्झना बारम्बार आउने, निद्रामा समस्या हुने, सजिलै झस्किने र दोषबोध महसुस गर्नेजस्ता समस्या पर्न सक्छन् । मनोवैज्ञानिक रोजेनफेल्डले नरेशले आफूमा देखिएका लक्षण बढाइचढाइ गरेको संकेत परीक्षणमा नदेखिएको र उनको पीटीएसडीसम्बन्धी मूल्याङ्कनका लागि आफूहरूसँग बलियो आधार रहेको दावी गरे । नरेशले पत्नी ममताको शव भेटेपछि आफू अत्यन्त आत्तिएको, शरीर अनियन्त्रित रूपमा काँपेको र स्पष्ट रूपमा सोच्न नसकेको दाबी गरेका छन् । रोजेनफेल्डले यस्तो अवस्थामा व्यक्तिले आत्तिएर स्पष्ट निर्णय गर्न नसक्नु पीटीएसडीसँग मेल खान सक्ने बताए । तर, मनोवैज्ञानिकले नरेशको व्यवहारका सबै पक्षलाई पीटीएसडीका आधारमा व्याख्या गर्न नसकिने पनि स्पष्ट पारे । विशेषगरी शव टुक्र्याउने र त्यसलाई लुकाउने कार्यलाई पीटीएसडीले स्वतः व्याख्या नगर्ने उनको भनाइ थियो । उनले नरेशले त्यसबेला वास्तवमा के सोचिरहेका थिए भन्ने कुरा आफ्नै मूल्याङ्कनबाट निश्चित गर्न नसकिने र उनको बयान सत्य हो वा होइन भन्ने निर्णय जूरीले गर्नुपर्ने बताए । पीटीएसडीले हत्या अभियोगबाट उन्मुक्ति मिल्दैन नरेश भट्टमा पोस्ट ट्रमाटिक स्ट्रेस डिसअर्डर (पीटीएसडी) रहेको मनोवैज्ञानिकको निष्कर्षले उनको प्रतिरक्षा पक्षलाई केही सहयोग पुग्न सक्छ । प्रतिरक्षा पक्षले घटनाका बेला उनी गम्भीर मानसिक आघातमा रहेको र त्यसले उनको सोच्ने तथा निर्णय गर्ने क्षमतामा असर पारेको तर्क गर्न सक्छ । अमेरिकाको भर्जिनिया राज्यको कानुनअनुसार पीटीएसडी हुनु र कानुनी रूपमा मानसिक अस्वस्थताका कारण अपराधको जिम्मेवारी लिन नसक्ने अवस्था हुनु फरक कुरा हुन् । मानसिक रोगको निदान हुँदैमा अभियुक्तले हत्या गरेको भए पनि उन्मुक्ति पाउँदैनन् । त्यसका लागि अपराध गर्दाको समयमा आफ्नो कार्यको प्रकृति वा त्यसको गलतपन बुझ्न नसक्ने अवस्था रहेको प्रमाणित गर्नुपर्छ । यद्यपि, नरेशको मानसिक स्वास्थ्यसम्बन्धी अवस्थालाई जूरीले घटनाक्रम र उनको व्यवहारको मूल्याङ्कन गर्दा विचार गर्न सक्छ । दोषी ठहर भएमा पनि मानसिक आघातलगायतका परिस्थितिले सजाय निर्धारणमा भूमिका खेल्न सक्छन् । तर पीटीएसडीकै आधारमा सजाय घट्ने वा हत्या अभियोगबाट छुटकारा पाइने निश्चित हुँदैन । नरेशले अदालतमा ममताले आत्महत्या गरेको दाबी गरेका छन् । उनका अनुसार सन् २०२४ जुलाई ३० को बिहान उनले ममतालाई घरको सुत्ने कोठामा अचेत अवस्थामा भेटेका थिए । उनले ममतालाई बचाउने प्रयास गरेको तर सफल नभएपछि आफू आत्तिएको बताएका छन् । तर, ममताको शव व्यवस्थापन गरेको कुरा भने उनले अदालतमा स्वीकार गरेका छन् । शवलाई काटेर विभिन्न फोहोर फाल्ने ठाउँमा लगेर फालेको उनले बयान दिएका छन् । ममता हराएको भन्दै प्रहरीलाई जानकारी गराएका नरेशले यसअघि आफूलाई उनको अवस्थाबारे थाहा नभएको बताएका थिए । Virginia. Naresh Bhatt, who is facing charges in the US for the murder of his wife, Mamta Bhatt, has testified that he was abducted by a Maoist rebel group as a teenager and was physically and sexually abused. He made the claim during an ongoing hearing in a court in Virginia, US. Naresh, who appeared as a witness in his own defense in court, said he was abducted by Maoist rebels when he was 13-14 years old. He says he suffered physical, sexual, and mental abuse while under Maoist control for more than two to three weeks. Naresh said that the incident he experienced as a child still affects him mentally. He also stated that he feels bad when he talks about those experiences. During his statement, Naresh also said that he witnessed his aunt's self-immolation as a child and felt guilty for the disappearance of his brother. He recounted these incidents in an attempt to prove that he was not mentally healthy. Psychologist concludes that Naresh has PTSD Naresh's defense presented psychologist Dr. Barry Rosenfeld as a witness in court. Rosenfeld, after evaluating Naresh, concluded that he had post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). PTSD is a mental health condition that can develop after experiencing a severe traumatic event. Symptoms can include nightmares, flashbacks, trouble sleeping, irritability, and feelings of guilt. Psychologist Rosenfeld claimed that the tests did not show any signs that Naresh was exaggerating his symptoms and that they had a strong basis for his PTSD assessment. Naresh claims that after finding his wife Mamta's body, he was extremely scared, his body was shaking uncontrollably, and he couldn't think clearly. Rosenfeld said that in such a situation, a person's inability to make clear decisions due to panic could be consistent with PTSD. However, the psychologist also made it clear that not all aspects of Naresh's behavior could be explained by PTSD. In particular, he said that PTSD would not automatically explain the act of dismembering and hiding the body. He said that it was impossible to determine from his own assessment what Naresh was really thinking at the time and that the jury would have to decide whether his statement was true or not. PTSD does not exempt from murder charges The psychologist's conclusion that Naresh Bhatt has post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) may provide some support to his defense, which could argue that he was severely traumatized at the time of the incident, which affected his ability to think and make decisions. According to Virginia law, having PTSD is different from being legally incapable of taking responsibility for a crime due to mental illness. A diagnosis of mental illness does not exempt a defendant from murder even if he or she committed it. To do so, it must be proven that the defendant was incapable of understanding the nature or wrongness of his or her actions at the time of the crime. However, the jury may consider Naresh's mental health condition when assessing the events and his behavior. Even if convicted, circumstances such as psychological trauma may play a role in determining the sentence. However, PTSD alone does not guarantee a reduced sentence or an acquittal on the murder charge. Naresh has claimed in court that Mamata committed suicide. According to him, on the morning of July 30, 2024, he found Mamata unconscious in the bedroom of the house. He said that he tried to save Mamata but was unsuccessful and panicked. However, he has admitted in court that he had disposed of Mamata's body. He has given a statement that he had cut up the body and taken it to various garbage dumps. Naresh, who had informed the police that Mamata was missing, had earlier said that he was not aware of her condition.
